description:
Spec: draft-atwood-jmap-chat-00 commit 0783fc4 ("condition MessageRevision push on edit-history retention") + §Message editHistory.

Spec text: "Servers MAY limit retained MessageRevisions; when the server does not retain edit history, the editHistory field MUST be omitted from Message/get and Message/changes responses. The Peer/deliver edit payload's history visibility is conditioned on retention."

Current state: Message.edit_history: Option<Vec<MessageRevision>> exists in chat-types; MemoryBackend writes whatever the update_object path produces. There is no retention policy in the kit.

## Acceptance

- New ChatBackend method:
  ```rust
  fn retains_edit_history(&self) -> bool { false }
  ```
  Sync (not async) because it's a static deployment-policy flag, not a per-call decision.
- handle_message_get and handle_message_changes consult backend.retains_edit_history() once per call; if false, project Message objects to omit edit_history before returning (i.e., set edit_history: None on the way out)
- MemoryBackend defaults to retains_edit_history() = false. A test-only setter `MemoryBackend::set_retains_edit_history_for_test(bool)` flips it.
- Test: Default MemoryBackend (false) → Message/get response on a message that has stored edit_history → response omits edit_history
- Test: MemoryBackend with set_retains_edit_history_for_test(true) → Message/get response includes edit_history

## Out of scope

- Per-message retention bounds (server limits the COUNT of MessageRevisions kept) — that's a backend-internal storage decision
- Federation Peer/deliver edit payload conditioning (Layer E federation work)
- Migration of existing stored messages when retention flips (consumer responsibility)
title: Layer B: ChatBackend::retains_edit_history + Message/get and Message/changes handler integration
